messages:
rana (Eng-Platform): Pile-on: Customer asked for a "compat adapter" that lets v1 clients call v2 and get v2 features without changing SDKs. Sounds neat but raises billing/telemetry UX questions.

oliver (Console): From UX perspective we can't silently flip billing. If we translate a v1 path to v2 semantics we should surface that in the route row as 'adapter: active' and show counts of adapted requests.

meera (Telemetry): Key ask: add a tag on route_events 'adapted=true|false' and emit original_client_version. We should sample full headers for adapted requests (1%) because it's a likely source of regression.

dave (Billing): Billing corner: if an adaptation upgrades output (e.g., higher-cost model), who pays? Policy decisions: 1) default: attribute by declared header (client said v1) => bill v1 price, 2) conservative: bill by effective execution (v2) unless customer opts out. Both have pros/cons.

rana (Eng-Platform): Implementation idea: adapter has three modes: passthrough, annotate, and upgrade. Passthrough: no change, just route. Annotate: run v2 engine but mark adapted=true and keep billing path-based. Upgrade: run v2 and bill v2. We can expose mode per-tenant via console toggle.

oliver (Console): I like per-tenant toggle behind an enterprise feature flag. Console needs a small banner when adapter enabled: "Adapter active: some calls are routed to newer runtime; see attribution panel." Also show adapted-rate on the route chart.

meera (Telemetry): Telemetry impact: adapted=true will increase inference cost metrics. We need a dashboard tile 'adapted rate' and an alert if adapted_rate > 0.5% of total for high-volume tenants. Also log execution_model and billing_attr_source for reconciliation.

dave (Billing): We'll need reconciliation window and audit logs. If tenant flips adapter from annotate->upgrade, we must run a delta job that charges the difference or issues credits depending on policy. Ops wants this automated.

ci-bot: PR #6789 opened for telemetry schema: added fields adapted, original_client_version, execution_model. CI checks pending.

rana (Eng-Platform): Security note: adapter must not accept arbitrary client headers as claims. We only honor X-Client-Version if token signature validates, otherwise it's marked original_client_version=unknown.

oliver (Console): UX microcopy: "Adapter modes: annotate = runs newer engine but bills as before; upgrade = runs newer engine and bills at new rate. Toggle is per-tenant and reversible with 7-day reconciliation window." Any objections to that wording?

dave (Billing): Sounds OK but legal needs "reversible" clarified. Also include explicit consent step for upgrade mode.

meera (Telemetry): Ops requests: 0.5% sampling of adapted requests full headers for 14 days during initial rollouts. dashboard tile + heatmap by tenant.

rana (Eng-Platform): Rollout proposal: 1) Telemetry schema + console flag (internal canary) 2) Adapter in annotate mode in staging -> internal beta 3) Console toggle to small set of tenants (annotate) -> monitor adapted_rate & support noise 4) If stable, open upgrade mode opt-in for enterprise after legal/product signoff.

oliver (Console): I'll add the toggle UI and the adapted-rate sparkline. Will show a confirm dialog for upgrade mode that links to billing policy.

dave (Billing): I'll build the reconciliation job and the alert rules. Add me to owners.

rana (Eng-Platform): Owners: rana (adapter impl), meera (telemetry + dashboard), oliver (console toggle + diagnostics), dave (billing + reconciliation). Keep default off globally. Post updates here.

meera (Telemetry): Noted. I'll also add logs for adaptation decisions so support can answer "why was my request adapted?"

rana (Eng-Platform): Thanks. If we get a lot of product asks to auto-upgrade all tenants, we'll need a clear opt-in flow and a pricing FAQ. For now feature-flagged per-tenant only.
